{{Quote|Kleex? Ah, your droid relieved the durkii of this insect pest!|Mon Julpa, to Jann Tosh|<ref name="TNK" />}}
'''Kleex''' was the name attributed to a [[Species/Legends|species]] of small, [[Color/Legends|brown]] and yellow [[Insect/Legends|insects]] with a dark blue shell found on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of [[Tammuz-an/Legends|Tammuz-an]]. They were [[Parasite/Legends|parasitic]] creatures that provoked an anger-inducing itching in their unwilling hosts. Because of a kleex infestation, the normally docile [[durkii]] [[Reptile/Legends|reptiles]] could turn into aggressive monsters.

==Biology and appearance==
[[File:Kleex_shell.png|thumb|left|The kleex had egg-shaped, dark blue shells.]]
Kleex were small [[Insect/Legends|insects]]<ref name="Blog" /> shaped like an [[Egg/Legends|egg]] cut in half vertically. Their back was protected by a smooth-looking, dark [[Color/Legends|blue]] shell, and their distinctive anatomic features were all located on their underside. Kleex had four pairs of bifid [[Limb/Legends|legs]] and two pairs of [[Antenna/Legends|antennae]]&mdash;one of which was located just above the creature's two lidded [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] and was more inconspicuous. The eyes themselves had a white sclera and a small, black pupil. Kleex displayed a segmented belly, the color of which alternated between brown and yellow. A kleex was approximately the same length as the hand of a [[Tammuz-an (species)|Tammuz-an]], a [[Species/Legends|species]] of tall [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoids]].<ref name="TNK" />

==Behavior and intelligence==
[[Parasite/Legends|Parasitic]] by nature, the kleex often attached themselves to the tails of larger animals, such as the purple [[Reptile/Legends|reptile]] known as [[durkii]], and the itching they provoked would madden the host, causing it to twist and squirm.<ref name="PoT">''[[Planet of Twilight]]''</ref> When picked in hand, a kleex would only react mildly, closing its eyes and shaking its legs gently.<ref name="TNK" />

==History==
[[File:Artoo_and_Barney.png|thumb|200px|R2-D2 eased a durkii maddened by parasitic kleex]]
The kleex evolved on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of [[Tammuz-an/Legends|Tammuz-an]],<ref name="TNK" /> a double-ringed world<ref name="dbT">{{DB|location|tammuzan|Tammuz-an}}</ref> located in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref>
One [[Standard day/Legends|day]], in [[15 BBY/Legends|15 BBY]],<ref name="SON">{{InsiderCite|73|A State of Nelvana: Droids & Ewoks Adventure Hour Revisited|A State of Nelvana: ''Droids & Ewoks Adventure Hour'' Revisited}}</ref> the [[Prince/Legends|Prince]] of Tammuz-an [[Mon Julpa]] and his [[Human/Legends|Human]] friend [[Jann Tosh]] were thrown into a pit by [[Vizier/Legends|Vizier]] [[Ko Zatec-Cha]], who [[Zatec-Cha's coup d'état|attempted]] to take the throne. In the pit, an angry, kleex-infested durkii had been released. Tosh's [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droid]] [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]] quelled the creature's temper by removing the kleex from its scales. Once freed from the undesirable insects, the grateful reptile immediately stopped attacking,<ref name="TNK" /> returning to its normally docile behavior.<ref name="SWE">''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref> In [[13 ABY/Legends|13 ABY]],<ref name="TERC">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]''</ref> the [[holograph]]ic counterfeiter [[Liegeus Vorn]] compared three [[Starship/Legends|starships]] of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], dodging and twisting in [[Realspace/Legends|space]] while trying to fire at [[Galactic Empire/Legends|enemy]] vessels, to a group of durkii maddened by parasitic kleex.<ref name="PoT" />

==Behind the scenes==
The kleex first appeared in "[[The New King]]," the sixth episode in the [[Star Wars: Droids: The Adventures of R2-D2 and C-3PO|''Star Wars: Droids'']] animated television series,<ref name="TNK" /> which aired on [[ABC Television Network|ABC]] on [[October 12]], [[1985]].<ref name="TV.com">{{TVcom|url=shows/droids/episodes|text=Droids - Episode Guide}}</ref> Those bugs and their parasitic behavior were later referenced in ''[[Planet of Twilight]]'', a [[1997]] novel written by [[Barbara Hambly]].<ref name="PoT" />
